newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-North has A$2 bln to spend on iron ore.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-North has A$2 bln to spend on iron ore.

text.p: Forestry and mining group North Ltd said on Wednesday that it planned to spend about A$2.0 billion to raise its profile in the iron ore industry.
"Our strategy is to be a major player in the iron ore industry," Malcolm Broomhead, deputy managing director, told an industry conference.
Broomhead said North was looking at ways to upgrade its orebody deposits at its West Angelas and Robe River iron ore operations in Western Australia as well as in Canada.
He also said North was interested in possibly reopening a iron ore pellet plant at Cape Lambert in Western Australia.
"We are looking at ways to get that plant open," he said.
The rise in electric arc furnace steel-making technology, used in so-called mini mills, was providing growing opportunities to supply iron ore to direct reduced iron (DRI) projects, he also said.
The share of crude steel production produced by mini mills is forecast to rise to 40 percent by 2005 from the current share of 35 percent.
Broomhead said other Australian iron ore producers were also planning large rises in expenditure.
The Australian mining house said at the end of January that it would spend US$230 million to buy a 59.3 percent stake in Iron Ore Co of Canada, that nation's biggest producer.
North said at the time that the acquisition would give it access to United States and Asian mini-mill markets.
North's other assets include 68 percent-ownership of uranium miner Energy Resources of Australia Ltd, forestry and gold mining operations in Australia, as well as base metals mining in Sweden.
